notes:
- **Scrolling capture (Pro).** Press **Alt+Z**, then **L** (the size says **Scroll**), then click a window or drag a region inside the part that scrolls. A9 Snap scrolls it by itself with the mouse wheel (the pointer is parked in the middle of the area while it works and put back afterwards), takes a frame after each scroll settles, and stitches the frames into **one tall PNG** by finding the rows they share (row hashes, then a pixel check; the scroll bar at the right edge is ignored). It adapts how far it scrolls to how far your app moves for a notch. A **header or footer that stays put** (identical rows at the top or bottom of every frame) is kept once, not repeated.
- **It stops** when nothing moves any more (the end of the page; a page shorter than the area gives an ordinary picture and the toast says *nothing scrolled*), at the **height limit** (new Saving setting **Tallest scrolling capture**: 10,000, 20,000 (default) or 40,000 px; the toast says *stopped at 20,000 px*), or when you press **Stop** on the small bar, **Esc**, or the capture hotkey: everything captured so far is kept. If two scrolls in a row can't be lined up the bar says **Scroll it yourself, then press Stop** and stitching carries on from your own scrolling.
- **It is an ordinary capture:** the clipboard, the next numbered PNG, the strip, the toast with **Edit**. **S** (secure capture) combines with **L**; **L** replaces **R** (record). Without Pro, **L** shows *Scrolling capture is part of A9 Snap Pro* and the capture is a normal picture; the Pro sheet opens once. The picker's hint gains **L scroll (Pro)**, and the Pro features page lists Scrolling capture as **Included** with how to use it.
- It works best in browsers and most lists and documents; some apps scroll in ways that can't be stitched (pages that animate or change while they scroll, apps that ignore the mouse wheel). New manual page **Scrolling capture**; Keyboard shortcuts, Settings, Pro features, Take a screenshot and Privacy cover it. Nothing is uploaded; the log says how many frames and how big, never what was in them.
